GaN strain, polarization, and atomic recoil modeling for neutron-detector research

  • Lead the simulation subteam within Georgia Tech's VIP partnership with Sandia National Laboratories.
  • Contribute to Quantum ESPRESSO strain-polarization calculations and LAMMPS recoil simulations.
  • Assess numerical convergence, local strain, and the physical limits of detector models.

I lead the simulation subteam in Georgia Tech's Compound Semiconductor Products VIP partnership with Sandia National Laboratories. Our modeling connects GaN strain and polarization with atomic recoil dynamics through Quantum ESPRESSO calculations and LAMMPS simulations. Static material-response calculations, controlled recoil studies, and time-step and cell-size checks establish the numerical basis for evaluating detector concepts. The scope is material response and detector feasibility, with electrical detection performance dependent on device geometry, bias, source conditions, and readout.

C / PERSONAL PROJECTS

Last Label / When should learning stop?

Python / small-text / scikit-learn

Annotation cost and predictive performance under noisy labels and biased stop sets

  • Evaluated published SP and PCF stopping rules across 15,360 learning trajectories on six binary tasks.
  • Analyzed paired cost-performance differences, budget fallbacks, noise interactions, and stopping-convention sensitivity.

Loading saved experiment...

LastLabel is an independent empirical study inspired by my earlier work with Dr. Michael Bloodgood. It evaluates methods by Bloodgood and his coauthors using small-text, simulated annotation noise, and alternative stop sets. The completed study includes 15,360 trajectories, paired uncertainty estimates, budget and sampling ablations, and a technical report. Annotation savings sometimes accompany lower predictive performance, while some equal outcomes reflect shared budget fallback. Four text tasks share one corpus, and the findings are descriptive rather than a universal ranking or a new stopping algorithm. Study release and reproducible results ↗

SENSORLAB / Learning where to measure

Thermal inference / Experimental design

Research concept: sensor placement for thermal-property inference

  • Research question: how does measurement location affect thermal-property recovery?
  • Study design: adaptive, uniform, and random layouts with matched measurement budgets.

SENSORLAB is a research concept centered on the relationship between sensor placement and thermal-property recovery. Its proposed experimental design pairs a differentiable heat model with adaptive, uniform, and random measurement layouts under equal budgets. The central questions concern parameter error, uncertainty, and identifiability from sparse observations.

LUMEN / CPU and GPU path tracer

C++ / CUDA / OpenGL

Path tracing for physically based lighting simulation

  • Built a multithreaded CPU path tracer with BVH traversal, area lights, and multiple importance sampling.
  • Implemented a CUDA wavefront backend and progressive OpenGL viewer.

LUMEN is a physically based path tracer for procedural scenes containing diffuse surfaces, ideal mirrors, and glass. Its multithreaded C++ renderer combines BVH traversal, area-light sampling, and multiple importance sampling. Deterministic sample streams and linear image output support reproducible error comparisons. The implementation also includes a CUDA wavefront backend and an OpenGL frontend for progressively displaying CPU renders. Source code and rendering benchmarks ↗
